modules.title: Baseline Assessment and Product Scope
outcomes: Identify transferable backend skills and specific gaps.
Define users, requirements, failure cases, and acceptance evidence.
reading: C1: Planning AI Applications, printed pp.28–34; The AI Engineering Stack, pp.35–46. Read selectively.
F2: consult project structures only after the first endpoint; avoid premature architecture.
exercises: Explain a JWT/RBAC flow, Zod validation, and an integration test from CRM. Write a typed JSON cleaner and a test without AI.
Write five user stories and three failure cases: missing evidence, unreadable document, and unauthorized resource access.
Choose a small permitted corpus, specify input/output contracts and three non-goals, and create the first ADR.
evidence: baseline.md with links to prior work
project-scope.md and the first ADR
modules.gate: Explain the use case and the first deliverable in two minutes. Review only demonstrated gaps rather than restarting backend fundamentals.
defer: Repeating JavaScript, HTTP, Git, or Docker basics after passing diagnostics
Microservices or buying a GPU before a need exists
exercise_checks: Record demonstrated skills and gaps; distinguish prior evidence from assumptions.
Each story has an observable acceptance condition.
A one-page scope and ten initial questions are sufficient to start building.

modules.title: Python, FastAPI, and Service Testing
outcomes: Use type hints, Pydantic, dependency injection, and lifespan management.
Separate HTTP handlers from application logic and test the service.
reading: F2, PDF43–82: server, Depends, lifespan, and project structure; skim familiar framework comparisons.
F4, PDF153–186: annotations, Annotated, Pydantic validators, serialization, and settings; skim primitive types.
F11, PDF500–518: pytest, fixtures, parameterization, async tests, and mocking; revisit as needed.
FastAPI documentation: types, request/response models, dependencies, and testing.
exercises: Implement /health and POST /reflect with an explicitly fake provider. Test valid, missing, invalid, and provider-timeout cases.
Write a context manager for a resource and a generator for batched records.
Replace the provider using a dependency override.
Explain annotations versus runtime validation and def versus async def. Add one endpoint without copying a solution.
evidence: Application skeleton in a separate implementation repository
Tests, pinned dependencies, and setup instructions
modules.gate: A clean checkout runs the API and tests. Provider failures have defined responses, and you can add and test a small feature independently.
defer: A complete Python beginner course if diagnostics pass
Agent frameworks and elaborate class hierarchies
exercise_checks: Tests make no live model calls and assert documented responses.
An exception triggers cleanup; batches preserve the expected records.
The API contract stays the same when fake and real adapters are swapped.
Demonstrate the distinction with a failing validation case; deepen concurrency in L10.

modules.title: Practical Mathematics, ML, and Data Preparation
outcomes: Understand vectors, matrices, similarity, probability, loss, and gradients through small examples.
Run an ML baseline with correct splits, preprocessing, and evaluation.
Recognize leakage and distinguish a similarity score from a calibrated probability.
reading: G1, printed pp.9–22, and C2 pp.58–87: conceptual orientation, not a complete ML curriculum.
C3 pp.125–135: functional correctness, similarity, and embeddings.
C8 pp.368–371 and 396–402: quality and processing principles.
Required gap resource: scikit-learn Common Pitfalls; consult split, preprocessing, and metric documentation for the lab.
exercises: Calculate dot products, norms, and cosine for [1,0] and [0,1]; implement zero-vector handling and explain matrix shapes.
Build a confusion matrix from eight predictions and calculate precision, recall, and F1.
Train a small logistic regression or decision tree on public toy or synthetic data; compare a majority baseline.
Create an intentionally leaky experiment, then repair it.
Explain a small loss curve, gradient descent, overfitting, and regularization.
evidence: math-notes.md and a small reproducible ML script or notebook
Leakage comparison with data source or generation seed
modules.gate: Compute simple similarity and classification metrics, explain train/validation/test, and reproduce the ML experiment without leaking test information.
defer: A full Data Science specialization
Advanced proofs or prolonged competition tuning
exercise_checks: Check orthogonal-vector similarity, identical-vector similarity, and the zero-vector policy.
Show denominators and handling of undefined cases; explain what each metric misses.
Fit preprocessing only on training data; save split, seed, and metrics.
Identify the leaked information and reproduce both configurations; no target score is required.
Describe the direction of an update and the difference between training and generalization.

modules.title: Deep Learning, Foundation Models, and Serving
outcomes: Distinguish pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, preference tuning, and inference.
Understand layers, autograd, attention, tokenization, sampling, and resource constraints.
Choose an external provider or local inference endpoint with a reasoned boundary.
reading: G1, printed pp.1–22: conceptual reading; skim material already understood.
C2 pp.49–111: skim architecture/post-training; focus on sampling and structured outputs, pp.88–105.
F3 PDF83–105 for language models and PDF136–150 for serving strategies; defer multimodal examples.
PyTorch Tensors and Autograd quickstarts: one tiny CPU lab.
exercises: Implement a tiny linear layer, loss, backward pass, and optimizer step in PyTorch.
Explore tokenization for representative inputs, optionally including Arabic and English.
Run five prompts using two sampling settings on one model.
Draw client → FastAPI → provider and compare external versus local serving.
evidence: tiny-autograd.py and tokenization observations
Model selection card and serving ADR
modules.gate: Explain next-token prediction and attention conceptually, demonstrate the autograd lab, and run inference. L02 may proceed in parallel; completing all ML topics is not a prerequisite for the first model API call.
defer: Training a transformer from scratch
Audio/video/3D serving and distributed GPU training
exercise_checks: Record tensor shapes, inspect gradients, and explain the update. Use L02 exercise E1 first if vectors are unfamiliar.
Distinguish characters, tokens, context capacity, and embedding dimensions.
Record settings and variation; low temperature is not treated as a determinism guarantee.
Document timeouts, lifecycle, privacy/resource constraints, and actual hardware assumptions.

modules.title: Prompt Engineering, Structured Outputs, and LLM Integration
outcomes: Design instructions, examples, schemas, and untrusted-input boundaries.
Integrate one model behind an adapter with controlled error handling.
reading: G2: What if we coded it?, printed pp.42–45; skip Langflow setup.
G3 pp.48–56 and 68–72: prompt quality, techniques, and the coding explanation.
F3 external serving, F4 validation, and F5 PDF203–208 provider APIs.
C5 pp.218–234: context efficiency and prompt versioning; C2 structured outputs as needed.
exercises: Use the supplied synthetic excerpts to return an answer and references drawn from a supplied ID list.
Test valid JSON containing a wrong claim, malformed output, timeout, and HTTP429.
Compare zero-shot with two few-shot examples on ten cases.
Implement bounded retries for selected transient failures.
evidence: Provider adapter, versioned prompt, and structured-output tests
Small prompt comparison report
modules.gate: No secrets are committed. Valid JSON is not mistaken for a correct answer. The same application logic works with fake and real providers.
defer: Many providers at once
Prompt frameworks or autonomous agent loops
exercise_checks: Validate the response schema on the server and reject unknown reference IDs.
Separate schema failure, factual failure, and transport failure.
Save prompt/model versions, usage, latency, and the observed differences.
Permanent failures do not loop; time and attempt limits are tested.

modules.title: Evaluation Engineering
outcomes: Define datasets and rubrics before expanding the application.
Distinguish deterministic tests, component evaluation, and end-to-end quality.
reading: C4 pp.200–207: Design Your Evaluation Pipeline; introduce during L00 and implement here.
C3 pp.114–117 and 125–147: challenges, exact evaluation, AI judges, and limitations.
C4 pp.160–178: criteria; F11 PDF495–533: model testing and retrieval/behavioral evaluation.
exercises: Use the twelve public seed cases for practice and author thirty development cases.
Create a separate holdout before tuning; label document/page/spans.
Write 0–2 rubrics for correctness, groundedness, and relevance.
Define an evaluation run manifest.
Specify retrieval and tool metrics before those components are built.
evidence: Authored evaluation data, rubric, and run manifest
A report showing real failures as well as successes
modules.gate: Explain what success means and why. Public seed data is not holdout, mocks do not assess model quality, and judges are not the sole source of truth.
defer: An elaborate evaluation platform before useful labels
Repeated tuning against the final holdout
exercise_checks: Include answerable, no-answer, multi-evidence, language, and security categories; review labels manually.
Do not call supplied examples unseen; preserve labels when chunk IDs change.
Calibrate a model judge against human review and document disagreements.
Record dataset/model/prompt/corpus versions, case count, latency, and cost or usage.
Implement retrieval metrics in L08 and tool/task metrics in L12; do not claim these experiments are already complete.

modules.title: PostgreSQL, ORM, and AI Application State
outcomes: Move from Mongoose-style ODM experience to SQLAlchemy relations, sessions, transactions, and Alembic.
Design document, conversation, and journal ownership and versions.
reading: F7 PDF302–337: ORM, engine/session lifecycle, CRUD, and schema migration; skim database comparisons and Prisma.
SQLAlchemy asyncio and Alembic official documentation as needed.
F8 authorization integration is applied in L11.
exercises: Design documents, chunks, conversations, messages, and journals with ownership and relational constraints.
Write an initial migration and a version-column migration; simulate a failed write.
Implement a session lifecycle per request/task.
Compare a direct SQL query with the ORM equivalent and add pagination.
evidence: ERD, migrations, and real-database integration tests
Session/transaction lifecycle note
modules.gate: Rebuild the schema from an empty database and prevent partial writes. Explain where transactions begin and end.
defer: Multiple databases without a requirement
Repeating SQL or MongoDB fundamentals already demonstrated
exercise_checks: Produce an ERD and explain keys, nullability, uniqueness, and ownership boundaries.
A fresh database migrates successfully; transaction rollback leaves consistent state.
Concurrent tasks do not share one mutable session; cleanup is tested.
Explain generated joins and index choices without relearning basic SQL.

modules.title: RAG Document Preparation, Embeddings, and Semantic Search
outcomes: Convert a small textual PDF into traceable chunks with page provenance.
Compare a lexical baseline with embeddings appropriate to the application language.
reading: G4 printed pp.74–82; C6 pp.257–266: retrieval foundations.
F5 PDF212–239: document ingestion/RAG; C8 pp.396–402: processing principles adapted to the corpus.
pgvector official documentation: exact search and filtering first; ANN later if measured need exists.
exercises: Start with the JSONL corpus, then a permitted 20–50-page text PDF.
Handle empty, corrupt, and scanned PDFs explicitly.
Compare two chunk configurations and version the embedding setup.
Implement a keyword baseline and exact vector retrieval.
Reprocess an identical file and an updated version.
evidence: Ingestion functions or CLI, corpus manifest, and provenance tests
Lexical and dense retrieval baseline
modules.gate: Every chunk maps to its source. Reprocessing is safe, embedding dimensions match storage, and the implementation remains small enough to debug.
defer: Distributed processing without scale
Premature ANN or OCR
exercise_checks: Preserve PDF page, printed label if available, and offsets before cleaning.
Unsupported inputs have a clear failure reason rather than an empty ready index.
Save chunker, document, model, and dimension; never mix incompatible embedding spaces.
Evaluate representative queries, including cross-language cases if they belong to the product scope.
No duplicate chunks, no partially published version, and a clear deletion contract for L11.

modules.title: RAG Systems, Citations, and Retrieval Improvement
outcomes: Build retrieval → context → generation with verifiable citations.
Diagnose failures and justify hybrid search or reranking through comparison.
reading: G4 printed pp.94–100: improvements and coding explanation.
F5 RAG and F11 PDF519–527 retrieval integration.
C6 pp.253–274, especially pp.267–272; C4 component evaluation.
exercises: Generate an evidence whitelist, validate references, and display server-provided source/page/snippet.
Measure hit@5 and recall@5 using evidence labels; run generation with oracle context.
Compare lexical and dense retrieval; trial one hybrid/RRF or reranker approach if justified.
Change one chunking or top-k setting at a time.
Test no-answer, contradictory sources, and an existing but irrelevant citation.
evidence: Measured RAG MVP and citation contract tests
Before/after report and failure taxonomy
modules.gate: Explain five failures using evidence. References both exist and support the answer under review. Report thresholds as your project targets, not official ITI standards.
defer: Agentic retrieval before a measured baseline
Fine-tuning as a parser repair strategy
exercise_checks: Reject invented IDs and review whether cited passages actually support claims.
Distinguish parsing, retrieval, and generation failures.
Keep the same dataset and report quality, latency, and cost differences.
Save fixed settings and negative results rather than presenting only wins.
The system does not invent support; similarity is not interpreted as answer confidence.

modules.title: Context Engineering, Memory, and Conversations
outcomes: Budget instructions, evidence, selected journals, history, and memory.
Manage memory provenance, correction, deletion, and summarization loss.
reading: Anthropic: context selection/retrieval and long-horizon sections.
C5 pp.218–219; C6 Memory pp.300–304; C10 Enhance Context p.450.
exercises: Write a context contract with source priorities and a token budget.
Compare focused evidence against longer distractor-heavy context.
Add journal CRUD and connect a user-selected entry to source passages.
Store explicit memory items with owner, source, date, edit, and delete.
Trial compaction on a long synthetic conversation.
evidence: Context contract, journal workflow, and editable memory schema
Focused-context and optional compaction experiments
modules.gate: Explain what entered context and why. Deletion is respected and stale summaries are not silently treated as facts.
defer: Uneditable automatic memory
Sub-agents before a working bounded single-agent design
exercise_checks: Show how each input is selected, bounded, and truncated.
Use the same tasks and measure effects rather than assuming more context helps.
Clearly separate source claims, journal facts, and assistant suggestions.
Do not infer permanent personality traits automatically; changes affect active context.
Compare required facts before/after and retain source links and covered message ranges; JIT tools arrive in L12.

modules.title: Concurrency, Streaming, and Long-Running Jobs
outcomes: Separate I/O concurrency from CPU parallelism and avoid blocking the event loop.
Handle streaming cancellation, timeouts, and restartable ingestion jobs.
reading: F5 PDF187–211 and 253–256; defer GPU-oriented inference internals.
F6 PDF258–301: streaming/SSE and communication tradeoffs.
FastAPI async/background tasks; Celery task semantics when durable execution is required.
exercises: Run five concurrent fake I/O requests and probe /health while work is pending.
Implement streaming with a final structured metadata event.
Define queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled job states and ownership.
Choose one queue if durability is needed and specify acknowledgment/retry/backoff.
evidence: Concurrency experiment, streaming tests, and job lifecycle
Replay and crash-recovery evidence
modules.gate: Light endpoints remain responsive during I/O waits. Partial output is not presented as complete success, and failed indexing never replaces a ready version.
defer: Additional messaging/workflow platforms without a requirement
WebSockets solely because token streaming is needed
exercise_checks: Demonstrate a blocking mistake and a suitable correction; async alone does not solve CPU-heavy parsing.
Test disconnect, partial provider failure, time limits, and cleanup.
Replay duplicate messages and restart a worker without duplicating chunks.
Test actual crash behavior; BackgroundTasks is not a durable queue and exactly-once is not assumed.

modules.title: Security, Authorization, and Responsible AI
outcomes: Enforce ownership before retrieval, source viewing, history, memory, and job access.
Constrain untrusted content, tools, uploads, and consumption.
reading: F8 PDF338–400: FastAPI authorization implementation; skim familiar JWT concepts.
OWASP GenAI Prompt Injection: server-enforced permissions and least privilege.
exercises: Build an A/B access matrix across every resource endpoint, source viewer, cache, and job state.
Index a passage that tries to change instructions or expose another journal.
Set file/page/token/request/tool/retry limits.
Delete a document and its derived data, memory links, and caches.
Threat-model upload/storage/provider/logs/tools and use synthetic journals.
evidence: Threat model, authorization integration tests, and security matrix
Deletion and retention policy
modules.gate: Pass designed isolation tests before public deployment. Passing tests is not proof of universal security; retrieved text does not grant tool privileges.
defer: System prompts as authorization controls
Unapproved autonomous write tools
exercise_checks: User B cannot retrieve, read, edit, or delete user A data.
Authorization remains independent of the model and document instructions.
Oversized requests and abuse have bounded, tested failure behavior.
Document active deletion and backup retention separately.
No secret or sensitive journal content appears in default logs or browser configuration.

modules.title: Tool Calling, Bounded Agents, and Multi-Agent Decisions
outcomes: Distinguish fixed workflows from model-directed tool loops.
Implement safe tool contracts and evaluate tool/task failures.
Understand sub-agent patterns without assuming they improve the product.
reading: G5 printed pp.102–107 and 122–127; G6 pp.130–132 for patterns, with implementation examples optional.
C6 Agents pp.275–299: tools, planning, and failure modes.
Anthropic: JIT context and sub-agent sections, interpreted through project experiments.
exercises: Define read-only search_passages and get_passage tools with bounded outputs.
Build a small direct-SDK loop with max steps, timeout, and token budget.
Compare a fixed workflow and agent on fifteen tasks.
Use lightweight references and fetch passages just in time.
Design a planner/worker experiment and a summary contract.
evidence: Tool contracts, bounded agent loop, and evaluation report
Single-agent versus multi-agent ADR
modules.gate: A model request is never treated as authorization. Loops stop predictably and you can justify either using an agent or retaining a fixed workflow.
defer: Framework orchestration before understanding a loop
Multi-agent implementation just to check a syllabus keyword
exercise_checks: Validate schemas and enforce authenticated ownership; no generic SQL or shell tool.
Handle unknown tool, invalid arguments, no-tool-needed, and repeated-loop cases.
Report success, tool errors, unauthorized attempts, latency, and cost.
Only permitted requested content is loaded; compare against upfront retrieval.
Implement extra agents only if a measured use case justifies isolation, coordination, and cost.

modules.title: MCP, Enterprise Integration, and AI Workflows
outcomes: Understand MCP host/client/server roles, primitives, transport, and authorization.
Build one bounded integration with explicit failure behavior.
reading: MCP official architecture and the chosen SDK version; the books are not a sufficient MCP reference.
C10 pp.472–473: orchestration; G8 conceptual reference only; C6 tool contracts as needed.
exercises: Contrast function calling with an MCP integration diagram.
Expose get_passage through a local MCP server and call it from one client.
Test malformed arguments, unauthorized documents, and timeout.
Design a reading-summary draft workflow with one simulated save operation.
evidence: Small MCP server/client demo and integration diagram
Version record and permission/timeout tests
modules.gate: Demonstrate one real tool invocation through a client and explain where permissions, context, approval, and retries live.
defer: Many MCP servers or invented enterprise integrations
Production remote authentication before a local protocol demonstration
exercise_checks: Identify who manages context and authorization; neither is delegated to the protocol.
Pin the protocol/SDK version and record successful discovery and invocation.
Connection failure does not widen permissions.
The application enforces approval, authorization, and duplicate handling for writes; no external message needs to be sent.

modules.title: MLOps, LLMOps, Architecture, and Deployment
outcomes: Version model/prompt/corpus/evaluation artifacts and trace execution.
Release, restore, and diagnose an AI service and its worker.

F11 E2E; C10 Monitoring and Observability pp.465–473.
F3 serving strategies and C9 performance metrics; GPU optimization remains optional.
exercises: Document application architecture and ADRs for inference, state, and worker boundaries.
Add trace IDs and stage timings for parsing/retrieval/model calls, TTFT, errors, and usage.
Build CI for deterministic tests and checks, with separately budgeted live evaluation.
Containerize and test fresh migration, persistent restart, backup/restore, and readiness.
Deploy once to a suitable environment or demonstrate a reproducible local operating setup.
evidence: Runbook, CI, release manifest, and traces
Deployment/local operating demo plus restore evidence
modules.gate: Reproduce a release, restore state, diagnose failure, and state operating limits. Docker alone is not production readiness.
defer: Kubernetes or multiple observability products by default
A GPU cluster before a measured serving requirement
exercise_checks: Explain failure boundaries and why a modular monolith is sufficient.
Sensitive content is redacted; representative failures can be located from a trace.
Model or prompt changes trigger an explicit regression review.
Record an actual restore, not just a backup command.
Test outage and rollback; public access requires HTTPS/auth/secrets controls.

modules.title: Model Selection, Cost, Latency, and User Feedback
outcomes: Improve a measured bottleneck without sacrificing quality or isolation.
Interpret user feedback as a signal rather than unquestioned labels.
reading: C4 Model Selection pp.179–200 and Cost and Latency pp.177–178.
F10 PDF429–476 selectively; C9 Performance Metrics pp.412–418.
C10 Feedback Design pp.480–489 and limitations pp.490–491.
exercises: Compare two model settings or models on the same workload.
Change context size, output length, or retrieval calls as one controlled experiment.
If caching is justified, define tenant/model/prompt/corpus keys and invalidation.
Classify synthetic thumbs/comments into style, factual, retrieval, and other failures.
evidence: Model scorecard, controlled optimization report, and feedback taxonomy
modules.gate: Every decision has a baseline, configuration, sample size, and limitations. Similarity is not answer confidence and feedback is not automatically ground truth.
defer: Semantic caching before invalidation rules
Many-model routing or GPU tuning without a bottleneck
exercise_checks: Report case count, quality, usage/cost basis, p50/p95, TTFT, date, and environment.
A latency win that breaks citation quality is not presented as an overall improvement.
Test cross-user isolation and deletion before enabling the cache.
Define a review loop; dislike is not automatically a factual-error training label.

modules.title: Capstone Release, Technical Defense, and Career Evidence
outcomes: Demonstrate a usable AI application with evaluation and operating evidence.

Draft evidence-based CV claims and a scoped freelance proposal.
evidence: Versioned release, demo, evaluation report/dashboard, and defense notes

defer: Waiting for every advanced topic before applying
Inflated metrics or unsupported production-ready claims
exercise_checks: Include failure paths and cross-user access tests.

Explain framework, model, retrieval, and single-agent decisions.
